security_audit.summary: The main static alerts are Markdown code fences and inline code, with many false positives. Several cited sections do provide real belt or npx commands, and the skill has an intentional external image-generation dependency that can send storyboard prompts or image references to third-party services.

remediation.suggestion: Keep only required belt commands in executable examples and move npx installation commands to a clearly marked manual setup section.
Add a privacy note that prompts, script details, and image references may be sent to inference.sh or FAL apps when using belt.
Pin trusted installation documentation and advise users to verify the CLI source before installing or logging in.

content.value_statement: Video teams need clear shot plans before production starts. This skill turns scene ideas into structured storyboard panels, shot lists, and visual generation prompts.
actual_capabilities: Defines common shot types, from extreme close-up to extreme wide shot.
Explains camera angles and camera movement choices for storyboards.
Provides continuity guidance for the 180-degree rule, eyeline match, match on action, and screen direction.
Shows a panel annotation format with scene, shot, movement, action, dialogue, sound, and music notes.
Outlines a workflow from shot list to generated panels and assembled boards.
Includes belt CLI examples for image generation and image stitching.
limitations: Generated panels require the belt CLI and access to external image-generation apps.
Image quality and character consistency may require manual selection and regeneration.
It does not replace director, cinematographer, or client review.
It does not provide production scheduling, budgeting, or call sheet tools.

use_cases.title: Plan a Short Film Scene
use_cases.description: Convert a written scene into a shot list with framing, movement, action, and duration notes.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Ad Concept
use_cases.description: Create storyboard panels that explain product moments, camera angles, and pacing for stakeholder approval.

use_cases.title: Map an Animatic Sequence
use_cases.description: Break an animation sequence into panels with continuity checks, movement arrows, and consistent visual prompts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Shot List
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a storyboard shot list for this scene: [paste scene]. Include shot type, camera angle, movement, action, and estimated duration.

prompt_templates.title: Turn a Script Into Panels
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this script excerpt into storyboard panels: [paste script]. Use scene and shot numbers, panel descriptions, dialogue notes, and sound cues.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Consistent Visual Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Create image generation prompts for this shot list: [paste shot list]. Keep one visual style across every panel and note any continuity risks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Storyboard Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete storyboard workflow for this video concept: [paste concept]. Include shot list, panel annotations, continuity checks, style guidance, and assembly notes.

output_examples.input: A character enters an empty office and finds a sealed envelope on the desk.
output: Scene 1 Shot 1: Wide shot of the office exterior in morning light, static camera, four seconds.
Scene 1 Shot 2: Medium shot as the character enters, slow dolly in, three seconds.
Scene 1 Shot 3: Extreme close-up of the envelope, no movement, two seconds.

output_examples.input: Plan a 30-second product ad for a smart water bottle.
output: Open with a wide establishing shot of a runner preparing before sunrise.
Cut to a close-up of the bottle lighting up with a hydration reminder.
End with a hero product shot and a clean panel note for music and logo timing.

output_examples.input: Review a chase storyboard for continuity problems.
output: Keep the runner moving left to right across consecutive shots unless a turn is shown.
Add a neutral shot before crossing the action axis between the runner and pursuer.
Use match on action when cutting from the jump wide shot to the landing close-up.

best_practices: Write the shot list before generating or drawing panels.
Use one style suffix across generated images to improve visual consistency.
Check the 180-degree rule, eyelines, match on action, and screen direction before assembly.
anti_patterns: Generating images before the scene goal and shot order are clear.
Using the same shot size for every panel in a sequence.
Sending confidential script details to external image services without approval.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images by itself?
faq.answer: It provides prompts and workflow guidance. Generated panels require a configured image tool, such as the belt CLI examples shown in the skill.

faq.question: Can I use it without the belt CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use it for shot lists, continuity checks, and annotations without generating images through belt.

faq.question: Which storyboard layouts does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers 2x3, 3x3, 2x2, and single-panel layouts for different planning needs.

faq.question: Does it help with continuity?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers the 180-degree rule, match on action, eyeline match, and screen direction.

faq.question: Is it useful for ads and music videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan short marketing spots, music video sequences, animation beats, and film scenes.

faq.question: What data should I avoid sharing?
faq.answer: Avoid unreleased scripts, client secrets, private names, and sensitive locations when using external image generation services.
